blocks.text: Unlike the OTC market where contracts are customized, Exchange Traded Currency Derivatives (ETCD) are highly standardized to ensure liquidity and safety.

items: Trading Unit (Lot Size): Fixed amount per contract (e.g., USDINR = $1000).
Quotation: How the price is displayed (e.g., in Rupee terms up to 4 decimal places).
Tick Size: The minimum price movement allowed (e.g., 0.0025 INR for USDINR).

blocks.text: Trading happens electronically on the exchange platform. Orders are matched based on Price-Time Priority (Best Price gets priority; if prices are same, the earlier order gets priority).
Exam Note: The trading hours for Currency Derivatives in India are typically 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
Currency futures in India are CASH SETTLED in Indian Rupees. There is no physical delivery of Dollars or Euros.

items: Daily Settlement: Profits/Losses are calculated daily (Marked-to-Market) and adjusted in the trader's account.
Final Settlement: Happens on the expiry day using the RBI Reference Rate.

blocks.text: Exchanges provide contracts for 12 near calendar months. The contracts expire 2 working days prior to the last business day of the expiry month.
Important: On the expiry day (usually a Friday), trading ends at 12:30 PM, not 5:00 PM.
